what.title: What is CQL?
what.content: CQL (Clinical Quality Language) is a standardized language developed by HL7 International, specifically designed for expressing clinical decision logic and quality measure criteria. It is a high-level, human-readable language that can be compiled into ELM (Expression Logical Model) for computer execution.

why.title: Why CQL?
why.problems: Before CQL, clinical quality measures and decision rules were mostly written in natural language, causing:
why.problem1: Inconsistent interpretation of the same measure across systems
why.problem2: Inability to automatically compute quality measures
why.problem3: Difficult rule maintenance, prone to errors
why.solution: CQL solves these problems: it is standardized, executable, and maintains human readability.

relationship.title: CQL and FHIR Relationship
relationship.content: CQL is a query language built on top of the FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) data model. CQL accesses clinical data through FHIR resource types (such as Patient, Condition, Observation) and performs logical operations on this data.
relationship.fhirModel: FHIR provides the data model (describes data structure)
relationship.cqlLogic: CQL provides the query logic (describes how to operate on data)
relationship.together: Together, they form a complete clinical knowledge expression framework

applications.title: CQL Application Scenarios
applications.ecqm: Electronic Clinical Quality Measures (eCQM) — Automatically compute healthcare quality indicators
applications.cds: Clinical Decision Support (CDS) — Real-time medication alerts and diagnostic recommendations
applications.phenotyping: Electronic Phenotyping (ePhenotyping) — Identify specific patient populations from EHR data
applications.research: Clinical Research — Define inclusion/exclusion criteria for study populations

library.title: Library Declaration
library.content: Every CQL file is a library that must begin with a library declaration, followed by a reference to the FHIR data model.
library.explanation: The library declaration specifies the library name and version, while 'using' designates the data model.

valueset.title: ValueSet & Code
valueset.content: A ValueSet is a collection of medical terminology codes used to filter specific clinical concepts.
valueset.explanation: ValueSets can reference external terminology server definitions (e.g., VSAC), or directly define codes.

context.title: Context
context.content: Context defines the scope of CQL operations. The most common is the Patient context.
context.explanation: In Patient context, all queries are automatically scoped to the currently evaluated patient.

retrieve.title: Data Retrieval (Retrieve)
retrieve.content: Retrieve is CQL's core operation for querying data from a FHIR server.
retrieve.explanation: The bracket syntax [ResourceType: terminology] queries FHIR resources matching the criteria.

query.title: Query Expressions
query.content: CQL supports rich query syntax including where filters, sort ordering, and return projections.
query.explanation: Query syntax is similar to SQL but designed for clinical data, supporting date intervals, terminology matching, etc.

define.title: Definitions (Define)
define.content: Define creates named expressions that can be referenced by other definitions, forming logic chains.
define.explanation: Definitions are CQL's core building blocks — each quality measure population corresponds to a define statement.

overview.title: Taiwan Core Implementation Guide Overview
overview.content: TWCORE IG is a localized implementation guide developed by Taiwan's Ministry of Health and Welfare based on HL7 FHIR R4, defining standardized data formats, terminology systems, and interoperability rules for Taiwan's healthcare information exchange.

profiles.title: TWCORE Profiles & CQL
profiles.content: TWCORE defines multiple FHIR Profiles, each adapted for Taiwan's healthcare environment. When writing CQL, we use the resource types corresponding to these Profiles to query data.

codeSystems.title: Taiwan Code Systems
codeSystems.content: TWCORE defines several Taiwan-specific terminology systems for encoding local healthcare concepts:
codeSystems.icd10cm: ICD-10-CM-TW — Taiwan International Classification of Diseases (diagnoses)
codeSystems.nhiMed: NHI Medication — National Health Insurance drug codes
codeSystems.nhiProc: Medical Service Payment — NHI medical service payment codes

example.title: Full Example: Diabetes Care Quality Measure
example.description: The following example demonstrates how to use CQL + TWCORE IG to define a diabetes care quality measure calculating HbA1c screening completion rate.

diabetes.title: Diabetes Care Quality
diabetes.description: Query diabetic patients' HbA1c test results using TWCORE Profiles to calculate control rates.
diabetes.explanation: This example demonstrates typical quality measure logic: defining population (diabetic patients), denominator (those who should be tested), numerator (patients with HbA1c < 7%). Uses LOINC code 4548-4 for HbA1c results.

hypertension.title: Hypertension Screening
hypertension.description: Query blood pressure measurements, identify patients with abnormal readings, and track medication usage.
hypertension.explanation: This example uses LOINC code 85354-9 (Blood Pressure Panel) to query BP records and compare systolic/diastolic thresholds. It also queries antihypertensive medications via MedicationRequest.

medication.title: Medication Safety Monitoring
medication.description: Monitor prescriptions, identify high-risk drug combinations and dose adjustment needs for renal impairment.
medication.explanation: This example combines MedicationRequest with Observation (eGFR) data to identify patients needing dose adjustments. Uses the NHI Medication code system.

encounter.title: Outpatient Visit Analysis
encounter.description: Analyze patient encounter records, calculate follow-up rates and ED-to-inpatient conversion ratios.
encounter.explanation: This example uses Encounter resources to query outpatient, emergency, and inpatient records, filtering by time intervals to compute visit statistics.

q1.question: What does CQL stand for?
q1.explanation: CQL stands for Clinical Quality Language, developed by HL7 International.

q2.question: Which data model does CQL use to access clinical data?
q2.explanation: CQL is built on top of the FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) data model.

q3.question: How do you query all Condition resources in CQL?
q3.explanation: CQL uses bracket syntax [ResourceType] to query FHIR resources, e.g., [Condition] retrieves all Condition resources.

q4.question: What is the compiled intermediate format of CQL called?
q4.explanation: CQL is compiled to ELM (Expression Logical Model), a machine-executable logical model.

q5.question: Which organization developed the TWCORE IG?
q5.explanation: TWCORE IG is developed by Taiwan's Ministry of Health and Welfare based on HL7 FHIR R4.

q6.question: What does 'context Patient' do in CQL?
options: Scopes queries to the currently evaluated patient
q6.explanation: 'context Patient' scopes all subsequent queries to the currently evaluated patient.

q7.question: Which terminology system is primarily used for diagnoses in Taiwan?
q7.explanation: Taiwan primarily uses ICD-10-CM-TW for diagnosis coding.

q8.question: What does the 'define' keyword do in CQL?
q8.explanation: 'define' creates named expressions that can be referenced by other definitions — CQL's core building blocks.

q9.question: What lab test does LOINC code 4548-4 correspond to?
q9.explanation: LOINC 4548-4 corresponds to Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood (HbA1c).

q10.question: What does eCQM stand for?
q10.explanation: eCQM stands for electronic Clinical Quality Measure, using CQL for measure logic definition.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting Guide
troubleshooting.subtitle: Common CQL errors and how to fix them

resolveType.title: Could not resolve type
resolveType.solution: Add the FHIR model declaration at the top of your library. This tells CQL which data model to use for resolving resource types.
resolveType.fix: Add 'using FHIR version '4.0.1'' after your library declaration

resolveContext.title: Could not resolve context
resolveContext.solution: Use the correct context name. Valid contexts are 'Patient', 'Practitioner', 'Encounter', or 'Unfiltered'. The most common is 'Patient'.

invokeMember.title: Cannot invoke member
invokeMember.solution: You're trying to access a property on a list instead of a single element. Use a query alias to access individual elements.
invokeMember.fix: Use a query: [Observation] O where O.value is not null

resolveCodeSystem.title: Could not resolve code system
resolveCodeSystem.error: Could not resolve code system name 'LOINC'
resolveCodeSystem.solution: Declare the code system before referencing it. Code systems must be declared with their canonical URL.

timeout.title: Translation Timeout
timeout.solution: Your CQL may be too complex. Break down large expressions into smaller define statements, reduce nested queries, or simplify logic.
timeout.fix: Split complex expressions into multiple simpler definitions

noResults.title: No Results Returned
noResults.error: All definitions returned null or empty results
noResults.solution: Check that your FHIR server has matching data. Verify date ranges in your Measurement Period, code system URIs, and value set OIDs match the data on the server.
noResults.fix: Verify data exists: check patient IDs, date ranges, and terminology codes

languageRef.title: CQL Language Reference
languageRef.subtitle: A comprehensive reference for CQL language features including conditionals, null handling, type system, date/time operations, and string manipulation.

conditionals.title: Conditional Expressions
conditionals.description: CQL provides two main conditional constructs: if/then/else for simple branching, and case/when for multi-way decisions. Both can be nested and combined with logical operators for complex clinical decision logic.
conditionals.keyPoints: Key points: if/then/else always requires an else branch. case/when supports two forms: general (case when condition then ...) and operand matching (case expression when value then ...). Both return a single value and can be used anywhere an expression is expected.

nullHandling.title: Null Handling
nullHandling.description: CQL uses three-valued logic (true, false, null) where null represents unknown or missing data. Understanding null propagation is critical for writing correct clinical logic, as missing clinical data is common in real-world healthcare systems.
nullHandling.clinicalExample: Clinical Example: Handling Missing Lab Values
nullHandling.keyPoints: Key points: null propagates through arithmetic (5 + null = null) and most logical operations. Use Coalesce() to provide fallback values. 'is null' and 'is not null' are the safe ways to check for null. The '&' operator is null-safe for string concatenation while '+' is not.

typeSystem.title: Type System
typeSystem.description: CQL has a strong type system with support for type casting ('as'), type testing ('is'), and conversion functions. This is particularly important when working with FHIR data, where elements like Observation.value can be polymorphic (Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, etc.).
typeSystem.keyPoints: Key points: 'as' performs type casting and returns null if the cast fails (safe cast). 'is' tests the type and returns a Boolean. Use conversion functions (ToString, ToInteger, ToDecimal, ToDateTime) for explicit conversions. The 'convert' expression provides an alternative syntax.

dateTime.title: Date/Time Operations
dateTime.description: CQL provides comprehensive date and time operations including construction, component extraction, duration calculation, date arithmetic, and interval membership testing. These are essential for clinical quality measures that rely on measurement periods and time-based criteria.
dateTime.keyPoints: Key points: 'duration in' calculates the number of whole calendar periods between two dates. 'difference in' counts calendar boundary crossings. Date arithmetic supports days, months, years, hours, minutes, seconds. The 'during' operator tests if a point or interval falls within another interval.

stringOps.title: String Operations
stringOps.description: CQL provides a full set of string manipulation functions for parsing, searching, and transforming text data. The null-safe concatenation operator (&) is particularly useful when working with clinical data where fields may be missing.
stringOps.keyPoints: Key points: Use '&' instead of '+' for null-safe concatenation. Substring() uses 0-based indexing. Matches() supports regular expressions. Split() and Combine() are useful for processing delimited clinical data. StartsWith() and EndsWith() are convenient for code category matching.

fhirpathElm.title: FHIRPath & ELM Guide
fhirpathElm.subtitle: Learn how CQL uses FHIRPath for data navigation and how CQL is compiled to ELM (Expression Logical Model) for machine execution.

fhirpath.title: FHIRPath in CQL
fhirpath.description: FHIRPath is a path-based navigation and extraction language designed for FHIR resources. CQL incorporates FHIRPath syntax for traversing resource properties, filtering collections, and testing conditions. Understanding FHIRPath is essential for writing effective CQL queries against FHIR data.
fhirpath.clinicalExample: Clinical Example: Navigating Complex FHIR Resources
fhirpath.keyPoints: Key points: FHIRPath uses dot notation for traversal and automatically iterates over collections. CQL extends FHIRPath with full query syntax (aliases, multi-source, aggregate, let, sort). Use .where() for inline filtering and .ofType() for polymorphic navigation. The .resolve() function follows FHIR reference links to retrieve referenced resources.

elm.title: Understanding ELM
elm.description: ELM (Expression Logical Model) is the machine-readable intermediate representation that CQL is compiled into. While you write CQL in its human-readable form, the CQL engine actually executes the ELM representation. Understanding ELM helps you debug translation errors and understand how the engine interprets your logic.
elm.keyPoints: Key points: CQL is always translated to ELM before execution. ELM is a tree of typed expression nodes (Retrieve, Query, FunctionRef, Property, etc.). Translation errors appear with severity, message, and errorType. Common errors include type mismatches (accessing list as single element) and unresolved identifiers (referencing undefined definitions).

ecqmTutorial.title: eCQM Development Tutorial
ecqmTutorial.subtitle: A step-by-step guide to building electronic Clinical Quality Measures using CQL, from understanding the structure to testing with patient data.

step1.title: Step 1: Understanding eCQM Structure
step1.description: An eCQM (electronic Clinical Quality Measure) is a standardized way to measure healthcare quality using computable logic. Each eCQM defines population criteria that categorize patients, and a scoring method that calculates the quality rate. The most common type is a proportion measure, which calculates the percentage of patients meeting a quality goal.
step1.keyPoints: Key points: Every eCQM has an Initial Population (IPP) that defines eligible patients. The Denominator is usually the same as or a subset of the IPP. The Numerator identifies patients who met the quality goal. Denominator Exclusions remove patients who should not be measured (e.g., hospice). Denominator Exceptions capture valid clinical reasons for not meeting the numerator.

step2.title: Step 2: Building a Proportion Measure
step2.description: Let's build a complete eCQM for 'Diabetes HbA1c Control' — measuring the percentage of diabetic patients aged 18-75 whose most recent HbA1c is below 9%. This is one of the most common quality measures in clinical practice.

step3.title: Step 3: Testing and Validation
step3.description: Testing eCQMs requires creating test patient bundles with known data and verifying that each patient falls into the expected population. A test case should specify the expected population membership (IPP, Denominator, Numerator, etc.) and include the minimum FHIR resources needed to evaluate the measure.
step3.debuggingTips: Common debugging issues: (1) Date ranges — ensure Observation.effectiveDateTime falls within the Measurement Period. (2) Missing codes — verify code system URIs and code values match exactly. (3) Status filters — check that resource status values match your where clauses (e.g., 'final' for Observations, 'active' for Conditions). (4) Reference links — ensure subject references point to the correct Patient resource.

step4.title: Step 4: Real-World Example — CMS146
step4.description: CMS146 (Appropriate Testing for Pharyngitis) is a well-known CMS quality measure that demonstrates multi-resource queries and temporal relationships. It measures whether children and adults diagnosed with pharyngitis received a Group A streptococcus test before being prescribed antibiotics. Below we examine the CQL logic and show how to map US-specific terminologies to Taiwan/TWCORE equivalents.
step4.keyPoints: Key points: CMS measures use US-specific value sets (VSAC) and drug codes (RxNorm). For Taiwan, map to ICD-10-CM-TW for diagnoses and NHI Medication codes for drugs. LOINC lab codes are international and typically work without changes. When adapting foreign measures, focus on terminology mapping while keeping the population logic structure intact.
